item.title: Connecticut golfer Ben James falls in PGA Tour playoff, still seeks first professional victory
item.description: Connecticut native Ben James plays his shot from the fourth tee during the final round of the World Wide Technology Championship 2026 at El Cardonal at Diamante on Nov. 8, 2026 in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. (Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) Connecticut native Ben James lost in a sudden-death golf playoff to Blades Brown Sunday at the PGA Tour's Wild Wide Technology Championship in Mexico. Brown birdied the par-5 18th hole after James missed a 6-foot putt for birdie. James, from Milford, was trying to win for the first time on the PGA Tour since turning pro in June. James, 23, holed a 20-foot putt for eagle on the par-5 18th hole in regulation to force the sudden-death playoff. Both players had eagle putts on the first sudden death playoff hole, which was the par-5 18th, but both missed and made gimme birdies to head back to the 18th tee again. Both golfers came up short with their second shots. James chipped first, hitting it 6 feet by the hole. "Definitely a lot of emotions," James told reporters. "I mean, it was a long day. I fought really, really hard. Really poor start, poor front nine. Drove the green on 10, three-putted. I couldn't really get anything going." James had a four-shot lead heading into the final round, but it was gone before he made the turn. He did share the lead a couple times during the back nine, but ended up two strokes behind Blades Brown while standing on the 16th tee. He failed to make birdie putts on holes 16 and 17, leaving it up to eagling the 18th hole. His 289-yard second shot with a 3-wood that landed on the green. He then made the 20-footer for eagle. "Had a feeling that it was going to go in. Hadn't really made anything all day," James said. "Just had a really good line on it and it was a good putt. Played the best I could." Brown had finished his round and was on the driving range when James made the tying putt. "Making an eagle on this final hole is no easy task," Brown told The Golf Channel. "I was hitting balls and saw he made it and I was ‘Alright, playoff, let's go'" I've known Ben since we were amateur golfers and he's just such an unbelievable player. He's lights out with the putter. I got him this time but I'm sure we are going to be battling out years to come." Brown skipped playing in college and turned professional at 17. He started the season on the Korn Ferry Tour then moved up to the PGA Tour. This is James' fifth top-10 finish since joining the PGA Tour in June courtesy of being No. 1 in the tour's University standings. He has missed the cut in just one event. James moved up to 53rd in the fall FedExCup standings. The top 60 qualify for the first two Signature Events for 2027. James has tour privileges through next year. A victory would have made him eligible through 2028. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. Get the biggest headlines of the day from our network of journalists around the state. item.title: Boston-based nonprofit Miles for Military honored during NFL Salute to Service events
item.description: A Boston-based nonprofit that helps active-duty service members get home to their families is getting some NFL recognition. Miles for Military was recognized alongside service members from Marine Corps Base Quantico as part of the Washington Commanders’ Salute to Service programming this weekend. The Commanders partnered with the nonprofit to provide flights home for four junior enlisted service members from Quantico. The organization also participated in the New England Patriots’ Salute to Service pregame festivities outside Gillette Stadium. The organization was founded in Boston in 2021 and has grown significantly as it works to connect military members with their families. Founder Maureen Byrne said the stories of service members helped by the program make the effort particularly meaningful. “It’s the most amazing feeling. The stories are just amazing,” Byrne said outside Gillette. The organization says the volunteer requirement is intended to make each flight part of a larger cycle of service, with military members giving back to communities before receiving assistance traveling home. item.title: Mike Vrabel gives blunt assessment of Christian Gonzalez's struggles
item.description: Mike Vrabel gives blunt assessment of Christian Gonzalez's struggles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Patriots had a number of problems in their 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday, but Christian Gonzalez was one of the most glaring. The fourth-year cornerback, fresh off a contract extension that made him the position's highest-paid player, struggled mightily as the Packers burned New England's secondary. Jordan Love was 10-of-11 for 187 yards and a touchdown when targeting Gonzalez, shattering the cornerback's previous career-worst mark of 74 yards allowed. After the game, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was clear that Gonzalez's level of play didn't meet the team's standard. Here's a look at Vrabel's comments and how Gonzalez explained his difficult day. MORE: 4 QBs who boosted their MVP chances in Week 9 Mike Vrabel gives blunt assessment of Christian Gonzalez's struggles Vrabel said the Patriots "expect a lot more" from Gonzalez after he struggled in Sunday's blowout loss. "When your best players don’t play good, you don’t have much of a chance in this league," Vrabel said. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else. It wasn’t just him." Vrabel took some responsibility, saying a lack of preparedness by the defense "starts with me," but he certainly didn't disagree with the assessment that Gonzalez struggled mightily. Both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden finished with more than 160 yards on Sunday, with 105 of Golden's yards coming while covered by Gonzalez. Some stats on Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez: - Today: 10/11, 187 yards, TD, PBU - Previous high yards allowed was 74 - Weeks 1-3: 6/17, 38 yards, 0 TDs, 4 PBUs - Weeks 6-9: 20/23, 324 yards, 1 TD, 1 PBU — Doug Kyed (@DougKyed) November 9, 2026 Gonzalez said after the game that he isn't planning to let the performance affect him going forward. "It’s not the end of the world," Gonzalez said. "I had a bad game, so I mean, I’m not shaken up by it. I’m not too worried about it. I’ll move on and be ready next week." Gonzalez signed a four-year, $135 million extension in September, after negotiations were one of the dominant storylines of Patriots training camp; the deal made him the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history. item.title: Watertown's Sam Mooney, Aberdeen golfers & Northern State athletes honored
item.description: Here's some recent sports briefs for Watertown and Aberdeen: Softball Sam Mooney of Watertown is one of three South Dakotans to receive the 2026 James Farrell Award of Excellence, one of USA Softball's highest honors for national championship hosts. Mooney is a USA Softball South Dakota men's slowpitch commissioner. Rick Graff and Dave Nielsen of Sioux Falls People for Youth also received the honor during the 95th USA Softball Council Meeting. The award recognizes tournament hosts who demonstrate outstanding leadership, hospitality and excellence in conducting USA Softball National Championship. Mooney was recognized for hosting the Men's Northern D National Championship in August at Watertown's PREMIER Softball Complex. Graff and Nielsen were honored for hosting the Northern A and B Girls Fastpitch National Championships this summer in Sioux Falls. Junior Golf Aberdeen Junior Golf Aberdeen has announced that Claire Crawford and Grayson Rehder has been selected as the recipients of 2026 Dean Shortridge Scholarship. Junior Golf Aberdeen annually awards two $1,500 educational scholarships to area high school seniors who have demonstrated involvement in golf and intend to purse education at a two or four-year institution. Crawford, a 2026 Aberdeen Roncalli High School graduate, played golf and basketball and received a number of other honors in high school. She is currently playing women's college golf at Dakota Wesleyan University in Mitchell where she is studying business administration with an emphasis on accounting and finance. Rehder, a 2026 Aberdeen Central High School graduate, played golf and tennis and also received a number of other honors in high school. He is now studying mechanical engineering at North Dakota State University in Fargo. NSIC Wrestling Northern State junior 125-pounder Sloan Johannsen of Watertown recently received the Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference Wrestler of the Week honor. Johannsen went 4-0 to win the 125-pound championship in Jimmie Open hosted by the University of Jamestown (ND). He recorded falls in the first two rounds and technical falls in the semifinals and championship. All-NSIC Volleyball Three Northern State University players, including sophomore outside hitter Katelyn Schroeder of Tulare and redshirt junior setter Ava Nilsson of Mansfield, have earned first team honors on the All-Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference volleyball team. Linnea Nesheim, a redshirt junior outside hitter from Sioux Falls, also earned the honor. Nilsson and Nesheim each moved up from the All-NSIC second team last year. Nilsson has recorded 1,208 assists, 254 digs and 38 aces; Schroeder 418 kills, 302 digs and 36 block assists; and Nesheim 2372 kills, 25 blocks and 171 digs for NSU, which opens play on Tuesday in the NSIC Tournament. item.title: Steve Sarkisian lauds the undeniable toughness of his Texas team
item.description: COLUMBIA, MO - NOVEMBER 07: Raleek Brown #0 of the Texas Longhorns tries to break free on a run in the third quarter of an SEC football game between the Texas Longhorns and Missouri Tigers on Nov 7, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Casting the entire football world as doubting the ability of the No. 7 Texas Longhorns to go into Columbia and beat the No. 18 Missouri Tigers is a real stretch , but it was much more believable when head coach Steve Sarkisian lauded the undeniable toughness of his football team after securing a fourth ranked win this season as the Longhorns navigate a nine-game SEC schedule for the first time. “The DNA of this organization is mental and physical toughness and I think that poured out of our pores today in this ball game,” Sarkisian said. Now through the fifth game in the eight-game stretch without a bye week to end the regular season, Texas is banged up, playing without three key starters and receiving just 18 snaps from star edge Colin Simmons in his return from a high ankle sprain. “If you’d have told me we walk in here without Trevor Goosby, without Cam Coleman, and a very limited Colin Simmons, with some other banged up receivers — by the way, those other three are probably going to go in the top 15 picks of the draft — I don’t know how many other teams could do that,” Sarkisian said. Texas did it largely by relying on the depth accumulated through years of highly-ranked recruiting classes, as well as key transfer portal additions stepping forward, like running back Raleek Brown, who caught the go-ahead touchdown pass on a wheel route and put the game away with his eight-yard rushing touchdown with 1:25 remaining. Of the 101 rushing yards gained by the three Texas running backs who played, Brown notched 86 yards on 17 carries. And while he didn’t break any runs longer than 13 yards, that was a credit to some solid situational tackling by Missouri more than the regular busts in execution and assignment from Kyle Flood’s offensive line, which somewhat steadied itself on Saturday. “One thing about Raleek, he might not be the biggest guy in stature, but he’s got a huge heart,” Sarkisian said. “This guy’s a very prideful player. item.description: San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw celebrates after recovering a fumble against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second half of an NFL football game in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. The three-man unit of Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw and Jaden Dugger has missed just one game this season after nine weeks, a far cry from the 47 games missed by the Niners' defensive line or the 34 games missed by Niners receivers. Unlike those other two groups, the singular absence was self-inflicted, not due to injury, with Greenlaw serving a one-game suspension on Oct. 19 for headbutting a Seahawks player on the sideline . Perhaps it was that consistent playing time that helped them dominate their visiting former Bay Area rivals. item.title: Patriots’ Disastrous Loss to Packers Exposes Troubling Reality About New England
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Patriots suffered a humiliating 45-27 loss to the Packers. Here’s what went wrong for Drake Maye, Mike Vrabel and New England, and what comes next. The New England Patriots spent much of the past month building confidence, winning football games and offering evidence that their rebuilding process was beginning to produce meaningful results. On Sunday, the Green Bay Packers tore through much of that optimism in one disastrous afternoon. Green Bay’s 45-27 victory at Gillette Stadium was more than a disappointing loss. It was a complete breakdown that exposed weaknesses on both sides of the football and raised uncomfortable questions about just how far the Patriots have progressed under head coach Mike Vrabel. Read Next Dianna Russini Nears NFL Media Return, Bringing Mike Vrabel Controversy Back Into Focus The numbers were staggering. The Packers rolled up 478 yards of offense, quarterback Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns, and New England committed four turnovers that Green Bay converted into 21 points. Perhaps most embarrassing, the 45 points were the most the Patriots have ever surrendered at Gillette Stadium, which opened in 2002. New England hadn’t allowed that many points in a regular-season game since 1993. And it happened on an afternoon when the organization was celebrating its championship history, with Tom Brady, Rob Gronkowski and members of the 2016 Super Bowl team returning to Foxborough. The contrast between the Patriots’ celebrated past and their present struggles could hardly have been more dramatic. Drake Maye’s Three Interceptions Put Patriots in an Impossible Position For weeks, Drake Maye had been one of the most encouraging developments in New England’s season. His improvement was a major reason the Patriots entered Sunday’s game with five victories and legitimate hopes of making a playoff push. Against Green Bay, however, Maye delivered the kind of performance that reminded everyone he remains a young quarterback with significant room to grow. Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards and three touchdowns, but those respectable passing numbers concealed a much more troubling performance. He threw three interceptions, all in the first half. The first came almost immediately, with Maye throwing into traffic on New England’s opening possession. Xavier McKinney intercepted the pass and returned it to the Patriots’ 14-yard line. Two plays later, Love scrambled for a touchdown. Before the Patriots could establish any rhythm, they were already chasing the game. Maye’s subsequent interceptions were equally damaging, including another McKinney takeaway that helped Green Bay extend its advantage to 24-7. The quarterback had thrown just one interception in his previous four games. He tripled that total in one half Sunday. There were positive moments. item.description: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love is one of the frontrunners for MVP after shining against the New England Patriots Sunday. Getty Images “MVP. MVP.” As Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love exited Gillette Stadium Sunday evening, the remaining fans in Foxboro told Love what they thought of him. “Man, it’s awesome,” Love said of the ‘MVP’ chants. “It’s definitely a very cool feeling to be able to hear fans chanting that.” Those fans are certainly onto something. Love had arguably the finest game of his NFL career and propelled the Packers to a 45-27 rout of New England, the defending AFC champions. Love was magnificent against the Patriots, throwing three touchdown passes and running for a fourth score. Love finished the game 23 for 29 for 372 yards and posted a 153.2 passer rating. Love threw a 5-yard touchdown to Matthew Golden, had a 10-yard TD strike to Savion Williams and a 39-yard scoring strike to Watson. Love also began his day with a 13-yard touchdown run and later added a two-point conversion run. The Packers have had a legendarily awful running game this season. The offensive line has been a mess. Green Bay’s wide receivers lead the league in drops. The Packers have one of the league’s worst kickers. And Green Bay entered Sunday with the second-most penalties in football. But Love has put the Packers on his back, is in the middle of a career year, and helped Green Bay improve to 6-3 following its rout of the Patriots. “Can’t ask for much more,” said Watson, who had seven receptions for 171 yards and a touchdown. “At the beginning of the year when we were going through not being the team that we wanted to be, (Love) was still doing everything that he could to play his best ball and doing everything he could. “To see him continue to stay even keeled throughout this season, whether it was a positive or a negative, you can’t ask for a much better leader or much better quarterback or much better driver of this offense throughout the season.” Golden, who had 10 receptions for 164 yards and a TD, agreed with Watson. “Phenomenal,” Golden said of Love’s play. “Just being able to play with a guy like that is a blessing. item.title: NFL Playoff Picture Week 9: Current Odds to Make the 2026 Postseason Ahead of Sunday Night Football
item.description: NFL Playoff Picture Week 9: Current Odds to Make the 2026 Postseason Ahead of Sunday Night Football The NFL playoff picture after Sunday’s late-afternoon games features six AFC teams with odds of 89% or better to make the postseason, according to PFN’s FPM simulations , and one seat left for everyone else. New England still holds it, but a 45-27 home loss to Green Bay dropped the Patriots from 72.2% to 57.7%, the steepest fall of Week 9 so far. Two games remain to reshape the board: Tampa Bay at Chicago on Sunday night and Buffalo at Minnesota on Monday night. Week 9 NFL Playoff Odds: The AFC’s Open Seat and the NFC North Logjam Jacksonville (99.4%), Buffalo (97.3%), Denver (95.8%), Cincinnati (95.7%), Kansas City (94.7%) and Pittsburgh (89.0%) have pulled ahead of the pack. Kansas City posted the week’s biggest gain so far, up 10.3 points after a 35-12 win over the Jets, and Cincinnati’s AFC North odds jumped from 44.4% to 59.6% after a 34-17 win over Atlanta in Madrid. Denver leads Kansas City 55.8% to 43.3% in the AFC West race, and idle Pittsburgh, at 36.5% to win the North, comes out of its bye with a trip to Cincinnati. Turnovers loosened New England’s hold on No. 7. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, two to Xavier McKinney, and Green Bay turned four takeaways into 22 points. “We haven’t had a clean, turnover-free game yet,” Maye said . The Patriots’ AFC East odds fell from 23.6% to 12.7%, leaving Buffalo at 87.3% to win the division before it plays. Cleveland (33.6%) is the only other AFC team above 20%. Todd Monken passed on a tying extra point with a minute left in overtime in New Orleans, and the two-point try failed in a 23-22 loss. “Tie or lose is what you’re saying there if you kick the extra point,” Monken said. A tie would have left the Browns 5-3-1, a half-game ahead of New England. San Francisco (98.2%) and Minnesota (95.8%) lead the NFC. The Giants, 5-2-1 after a 19-11 win in Philadelphia, rose to 85.0%, with an 83.8% chance to win the NFC East doing nearly all the work. The crowd starts in the NFC North. Chicago (79.3%), Detroit (76.0%), and Green Bay (69.8%) all trail Minnesota, and the four clubs combine for 320.9 percentage points, an expected 3.2 playoff berths from one division. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Green Bay’s 45-27 win, behind 372 passing yards from Jordan Love, opened a 22.8-point cushion on 5-4 Seattle (47.0%), with the 5-4 Rams at 26.8%. Minnesota visits Green Bay next, and Love kept his focus there. “You can’t let one game lull you to sleep,” he said. item.title: Bill Cowher calls for Browns to commit to Shedeur Sanders
item.description: Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images, CBS The Cleveland Browns have gotten off to a better start to the NFL season than anyone expected . The longtime basement dwellers of the league were 5–3 heading into Sunday’s showdown on the road against the New Orleans Saints. Cleveland had to make one significant change to the lineup before their game on Sunday, with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders stepping up to start due to Deshaun Watson missing the week’s worth of practice while in the league’s concussion protocol. The Browns ultimately lost to the Saints 23–22 in overtime, but Sanders showed enough skill to have Browns fans excited for what could be in store for their young quarterback, and even convinced some analysts that it was time for Cleveland to embrace the future. Speaking after the game, former Steelers coach Bill Cowher was adamant that the Browns should commit to Sanders under center full time, even if Watson were to be available next week. “I would just say this: Moving forward, Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team,” Cowher said. “He’s going to be the future. And I think what he showed today, his resilience, continued to come back. He made great decisions, he extended plays. I love the way he played and I would move forward with him.” When cohost Nate Burleson asked if Cowher believed Watson hadn’t played well enough to get his job back when healthy, Cowher said it was more important to look into the future. “One person’s unfortunate situation creates another person’s opportunity. I just think that right now, what I saw from Shedeur Sanders, I would move forward. Because he is the future of your football team.” “Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team. He’s gonna be the future.” – Bill Cowher https://t.co/UN78KLHXxX — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 8, 2026 While it might sound odd for a team to consider starting its 0–1 backup quarterback over its 5–3 starting quarterback when both are healthy, the game that Sanders played on Sunday showed why it might be worth looking into for the Browns. Sanders finished the game 297 passing yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. His QB rating was 114.6 on the day. In Watson’s eight starts this season, he’s cleared 270 yards passing just twice, thrown for two touchdowns just twice, and has never done both in the same game. Just one of his eight starts saw him record a QB rating in the triple digits. Further, Sanders was able to deliver in crunch time when the Browns needed him, creating space and throwing an impressive pass in the final minute to put his team in position to kick a game-tying field goal to force overtime. This play alone is better than anything Watson has done all year. Keep developing Shedeur. He’s the future. https://t.co/6udkhpSyqk — Brownies (@BrowniesToBowl) November 8, 2026 Beyond his play on the field, there’s plenty more extremely simple reasons the Browns might want to get a head start on the potential Sanders era.

item.description: Everyone knows by now that the Edmonton Oilers can't seem to keep their goaltenders healthy. Edmonton entered training camp with three goaltenders, and just 10 games into the season, two were injured, forcing the Oilers to use four different goaltenders and dress an emergency backup.
